data.narrative:
Credo Semiconductor is a public-stage company in Chips & Semiconductors, currently valued at approximately $35.8B following its 2022 IPO. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers in the same sector and stage (Cerebras, Ouster, Aeva Technologies), supplemented by a broader set of 8 private frontier-tech peers and 3 large-cap public semiconductor benchmarks.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The median valuation across the 3 same-sector, same-stage peers is $2.3B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Aeva Technologies) to $39.2B (Cerebras). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples cannot be applied, as Credo's revenue is not disclosed in available data. The public semiconductor universe (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) carries a median P/S multiple of 20.5x, but without target-specific revenue figures, this method yields no actionable result.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B to $2.6B, with a median point of $2.3B. The key uncertainty is the extreme dispersion within the peer set—Cerebras trades at 36x the valuation floor—reflecting heterogeneous business models and profitability profiles within frontier semiconductor ventures. Credo's current $35.8B public valuation substantially exceeds this peer-derived range, suggesting either material differentiation in financial performance not captured in the comp set or market sentiment premiums not yet validated by comparable metrics.
